stem: Proofread these three tokens: (1) embarassment, (2) embarrass, (3) harrassment. A batch tool offers commands applied once each in the stated order. G replaces every 'rr' with 'r' in every token. E replaces the WHOLE WORD 'embarass' with 'embarrass'. M replaces the WHOLE WORD 'embarassment' with 'embarrassment'. Commands use the text left by earlier commands. Which plan leaves ALL three tokens correctly spelled, including restoring any correct form damaged during editing?

choices.text: E, then M; do not run G.
G, then M; do not run E.

explanation: The required final tokens are embarrassment, embarrass, harassment. G repairs harrassment but changes the initially correct embarrass into embarass; E must therefore follow G. M repairs embarassment, but running G after M would damage the restored double r again. G-E-M succeeds. Without G, harrassment remains; M-G-E leaves embarassment; G-M without E leaves embarass. Thus every token affects the decision, and knowing one spelling alone is not enough to validate a plan.

stem: A batch contains the tokens 'accomodate', 'accomodation', and 'recommend'. An edit command replaces either one exact whole-word spelling everywhere or one literal letter sequence everywhere, as specified; it costs ONE command regardless of matches. Keep already correct spellings correct. Which plan corrects the entire batch using the FEWEST commands? Read each quoted replacement literally.
explanation: Accommodate and accommodation require double c and double m, whereas recommend already has one c and double m. The sequence comod occurs in both defective words; changing it to commod repairs both and does not occur in recommend. Zero commands cannot work, so one safe command is minimal. Doubling every m damages recommend; two correct whole-word edits work but are not minimal; accomadate is still misspelled; correcting only accomodate leaves accomodation defective. Five choices distinguish the three orthographic checks from the separate minimal-command requirement.
